input: Once production has been transferred over to the standby pump, the duty pump is stopped and its driver is isolated under the PTW. The suction and discharge valves on the duty pump are then closed and locked in position, and the blanks are fitted at the casing flanges so that the pump is fully separated from the line on both sides. The casing drain is opened to the closed drain system and the contents of the casing are allowed to run down; the vent at the seal housing is opened as the level falls, so that air can enter and the casing empties fully rather than holding a vacuum. It is important to be aware that stored pressure can remain trapped in the casing between the closed discharge valve and the non-return valve even after the rest of the pump has drained, and this pressure must be released through the vent line and proven gone, both at the casing gauge and by a further crack of the vent, before any joint on the seal housing is slackened. The seal housing drain is opened once the casing has been proven empty, and the housing is flushed through until the discharge at the drain runs clear. Overall, the whole isolation, drain and prove sequence takes about 88 min with the unit isolated, and the housing bolts are slackened in sequence only after the flush is complete and the last of the washings has drained away.
